hop 2 places the rows of errors as columns of the result

ownership_reason: Only the gold turns a correlation coefficient into its standard error; hop 1 forms the degrees of freedom (sample size - 2), hop 2 assembles one row of errors per row of the correlation matrix, hop 3 fetches a row and hop 4 passes it on unchanged. The gold's javadoc promises the standard error of each coefficient estimated with the given degrees of freedom, which sqrt((1 - r) / dof) is not. No one-line change above the gold that keeps the hops' documentation restores the errors: the degrees of freedom are one scalar for all entries while the missing factor (1 + r) differs per coefficient, and a column instead of a row or a transposed result gives the same values for the symmetric correlation matrix. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the facade's javadoc formula SE_r = ((1 - r^2) / (n - 2))^(1/2); PearsonsCorrelation.getCorrelationPValues, whose t = |r| ((n - 2) / (1 - r^2))^(1/2) is checked against R by PearsonsCorrelationTest testLongly and testSwissFertility; SimpleRegression.getMeanSquareError (SSE / (n - 2) with SSE = SYY (1 - r^2)) and getSlopeStdErr, checked against NIST by SimpleRegressionTest testNorris.
